senses.en: Northeast China (Heilongjiang, Jilin, Liaoning); on its own, 东北 usually means this region
northeast, as a direction or part of a place: 北京东北边 'the northeast of Beijing'

examples.zh: 我是东北人，不怕冷。
examples.en: I'm from the Northeast, so the cold doesn't bother me.
examples.analysis: 东北 here is the region, Northeast China. Place + 人 says where someone is from: 东北人 'a Northeasterner', like 北京人. 不怕冷 'not afraid of the cold' is the natural way to say the cold doesn't bother you.

examples.zh: 东北冬天有多冷？
examples.en: How cold does it get in the Northeast in winter?
examples.analysis: 东北 is the topic and 冬天 'in winter' narrows the time; both come before the comment, with no word for 'in'. 有多 + adjective asks 'how…?': 有多冷 'how cold (does it get)'.

examples.zh: 我住在北京东北边，你呢？
examples.en: I live in the northeast of Beijing. What about you?
examples.analysis: Here 东北 is a direction inside a city: the bigger place first, then the direction, then 边 'side': 北京东北边 'the northeast side of Beijing'. Chinese puts east or west first (东北 'east-north'); English puts north first. 你呢 turns the question back.

hook: 东 'east' + 北 'north'. Chinese names the east or west part first: 东北, 东南, 西北, 西南.

meaning: daily newspaper; (at work) a daily report

senses.en: daily newspaper; often part of a paper's name: 北京日报 'Beijing Daily'
(at work) a short daily report that staff send to their manager

measure.note: 一份日报 'a copy of a daily paper'

examples.zh: 我爸早上起来先看《北京日报》。
examples.en: The first thing my dad does when he gets up is read the Beijing Daily.
examples.analysis: 日报 is part of a paper's name here: 北京日报 'Beijing Daily'. Many Chinese papers are named place + 日报. 早上起来先 + verb means 'the first thing (he does) after getting up in the morning'.

examples.zh: 《中国日报》是英文的，你可以看看。
examples.en: China Daily is in English. You could take a look at it.
examples.analysis: 中国日报 is China Daily, an English-language paper. 是英文的 'is in English': 是 + noun + 的 says what kind it is. 看看, the verb doubled, makes the suggestion light: 'have a look'.

examples.zh: 今天的日报你写了没有？
examples.en: Have you written today's daily report?
examples.analysis: At work, 日报 is a short daily report for the manager. The object 今天的日报 comes first as the topic, then 你写了没有: verb + 了 + 没有 asks whether something has been done yet.

hook: 日 'day' + 报 'paper, report': a paper or report that comes out every day.

meaning: name (of a thing, company, product or group, not a person)

senses.en: name of a thing, place, organization or product; common on forms and labels

examples.zh: 这儿写公司名称，那儿写你的名字。
examples.en: Write the company name here and your name there.
examples.analysis: The contrast is the lesson: 名称 is the name of a thing or organization (公司名称 'company name'), while 名字 is the everyday word for a person's name. Two parallel halves, 这儿写… 那儿写…, mean 'here write…, there write…'.

examples.zh: 这个公司名称太长了，换一个吧。
examples.en: This company name is too long. Let's pick another one.
examples.analysis: 名称 here is the name of an organization being registered or written down. 太长了 'too long': 太 + adjective + 了. 换一个吧 'let's switch to another one' makes a suggestion; 一个 stands for 一个公司名称.

examples.zh: 你们小组的名称想好了吗？
examples.en: Has your group decided on a name yet?
examples.analysis: 名称 suits a group name that must be registered or written on a poster or sign-up sheet. In casual chat people usually say 名字 instead. 你们小组的名称 is the topic. 想好 = 'think' + 好 'settled', so 想好了 is 'have decided on'. 吗 makes it a yes/no question.

related.en: name; the everyday word, above all for people

senses.en: washing machine; washer

measure.note: 一台洗衣机 'a washing machine' (台 counts machines)

examples.zh: 洗衣机坏了，衣服还没洗呢。
examples.en: The washing machine's broken, and the laundry still isn't done.
examples.analysis: 洗衣机 is the subject: 洗衣机坏了 'the washing machine has broken', with 了 marking the change to a broken state. 还没 + verb + 呢 means 'still haven't…'; 呢 stresses that this is how things stand right now.

examples.zh: 你家的洗衣机在哪儿？我想洗几件衣服。
examples.en: Where's your washing machine? I'd like to wash a few things.
examples.analysis: Thing + 在哪儿 asks where it is: 洗衣机在哪儿 'where is the washing machine?'. 你家的 'your home's' says whose. In 洗几件衣服, 几 means 'a few', not 'how many', because that sentence is a statement.

examples.zh: 这件衣服别放洗衣机里，我自己洗。
examples.en: Don't put this one in the washing machine. I'll wash it myself.
examples.analysis: 洗衣机里 'in the washing machine': an object noun like 洗衣机 needs 里 to become a place. In speech 放 often takes the place directly, without 在. 别 makes it a 'don't' request, and 我自己洗 'I'll wash it myself' gives the plan.

senses.en: pharmacy; drugstore (a shop that sells medicine)

measure.note: 一家药店 'a pharmacy' (家 counts shops)

examples.zh: 请问，这边有药店吗？
examples.en: Excuse me, is there a pharmacy around here?
examples.analysis: Place + 有 + thing asks whether something is there: 这边有药店吗 'is there a pharmacy around here?'. 请问 'may I ask' opens a polite question to a stranger.

examples.zh: 我下班去药店，要我帮你带什么吗？
examples.en: I'm going to the pharmacy after work. Want me to get you anything?
examples.analysis: 去药店 'go to the pharmacy': 去 takes the place directly, with no preposition. 下班 before it sets the time, 'after work'. With 吗, 什么 means 'anything': 要我帮你带什么吗 'want me to get you anything?'.

examples.zh: 这个药药店买不到，得去医院开。
examples.en: You can't get this medicine at a pharmacy. You have to get it prescribed at a hospital.
examples.analysis: 药 'medicine' and 药店 'pharmacy' sit side by side: 这个药 is the topic, 药店 says where. 买不到 'can't get (it) by buying'. 开 here means 'to prescribe', so 得去医院开 is 'have to get it prescribed at a hospital'.

collocations.en: to buy medicine at a pharmacy

meaning: words and expressions; a term or expression

senses.en: words and expressions, as a group (in a lesson or text)
a word or set expression; a term

examples.zh: 这些词语你都会用吗？
examples.en: Can you use all of these words?
examples.analysis: 这些词语 'these words and expressions' is the object, moved to the front as the topic. 都 'all' points back at that group. 会用 'know how to use': 会 is for a learned skill.

examples.zh: 这个词语我没见过，什么意思？
examples.en: I haven't come across this expression before. What does it mean?
examples.analysis: 这个词语 'this expression' is the topic. 没见过 'haven't seen (before)': 没 + verb + 过 denies any past experience of it. 什么意思, with no verb, is the everyday way to ask 'what does it mean?'.

examples.zh: 请用这些词语写一段话。
examples.en: Please write a short paragraph using these words.
examples.analysis: A typical class instruction. 用 + thing + verb means 'use … to do': 用这些词语写 'write using these words'. 一段话 'a short paragraph': 段 is the measure word for a stretch of text or speech.

meaning: Have a good trip! Bon voyage!

senses.en: Have a good trip! (said to someone setting off on a journey)

examples.zh: 明天就走了？一路顺风！
examples.en: You're leaving tomorrow? Have a good trip!
examples.analysis: 一路顺风 stands alone as a complete wish, with no verb: 'have a good trip!'. 明天就走了 'leaving as soon as tomorrow': 就 stresses how soon. Asked with rising intonation, it shows surprise.

examples.zh: 到了给我打电话，一路顺风！
examples.en: Call me when you get there. Have a good trip!
examples.analysis: A typical goodbye: a request, then the wish. 到了 'once you've arrived' works as a time clause with no word for 'when'. 给我打电话 'call me': 给 + person comes before the verb.

examples.zh: 大家一路顺风，下次见！
examples.en: Have a good trip, everyone. See you next time!
examples.analysis: Here 一路顺风 follows 大家 'everyone', said to a group as they set off: 'everyone, have a good trip'. The fuller wish is 祝大家一路顺风. 下次见 'see you next time' closes the goodbye.

related.en: have a safe trip; some people prefer it for flights

hook: Literally 'the whole way (一路) with a following wind (顺风)'.

senses.en: fast food; a quick, cheap meal (burgers, but also Chinese set meals: 中式快餐)

examples.zh: 中午没时间，吃个快餐吧。
examples.en: There's no time at lunch, so let's just grab some fast food.
examples.analysis: 吃个快餐 'grab some fast food': 个 before the noun makes it casual, 'just a quick…', even though fast food isn't really counted. 没时间 'no time' gives the reason, and 吧 turns the plan into a suggestion.

examples.zh: 你别老吃快餐，对身体不好。
examples.en: Stop eating fast food all the time. It's bad for your health.
examples.analysis: 别 + verb is 'don't', and 老 here is an adverb, 'all the time', not 'old': 别老吃快餐 'stop eating fast food all the time'. 对身体不好 'bad for your health': 对 + thing + 不好.

examples.zh: 晚上吃快餐还是自己做饭？
examples.en: Shall we get fast food tonight, or cook for ourselves?
examples.analysis: 还是 joins two choices in a question: 吃快餐 'eat fast food' or 自己做饭 'cook ourselves'. 晚上 at the front sets the time, and the subject 'we' is left out because both speakers know it.

senses.en: a calendar month; number + 月份 names a month: 七月份 '(in) July'

examples.zh: 你几月份去北京？
examples.en: What month are you going to Beijing?
examples.analysis: 几月份 asks 'which month?', with 几 standing in for the number. The time word goes before the verb: 你 + 几月份 + 去北京. 几月 alone means the same; 几月份 is very common in speech.

examples.zh: 七月份这儿特别热。
examples.en: It gets really hot here in July.
examples.analysis: Number + 月份 names a month of the year: 七月份 '(in) July'. It opens the sentence to set the time and needs no word for 'in'. 特别 'really, especially' strengthens 热 'hot'.

examples.zh: 月份写错了，是五月，不是三月。
examples.en: You wrote the wrong month. It's May, not March.
examples.analysis: 月份 here is the month part of a written date. 写错了 'written wrong': verb + 错 'wrong' + 了. Then 是…，不是… corrects it. For a length of time, use 个月 instead: 三个月 'three months'.

collocations.en: this time of year (plain 'this month' is 这个月)

related.en: month; the shorter form, and the one used in full dates (五月二十号)

senses.en: sentence (a full sentence of speech or writing)

measure.note: 一个句子 (for spoken lines, 一句话 'one sentence' is also common)

examples.zh: 这个句子我不太明白。
examples.en: I don't quite understand this sentence.
examples.analysis: 这个句子 'this sentence' comes first as the topic, then 我 + 不太明白. 不太 'not very' softens the negative: 'don't quite understand'. Putting the thing first is a common way to say what you are talking about.

examples.zh: 你的句子太长了，可以写短一点儿。
examples.en: Your sentences are too long. You could make them a bit shorter.
examples.analysis: 太 + adjective + 了 'too…': 太长了 'too long'. 写短一点儿 'write (them) a bit shorter': adjective + 一点儿 after the verb asks for a little more of that quality. 可以 softens the advice to 'you could'.

examples.zh: 你能用这个词写个句子吗？
examples.en: Can you write a sentence with this word?
examples.analysis: 用 + thing + verb is 'use … to': 用这个词写 'write using this word'. 个句子 drops the 一 of 一个, as speech often does. 词 is a single word; 句子 is the whole sentence built from words.

collocations.en: to make up a sentence (with a given word), a classic class exercise

related.en: measure word for lines and sentences: 一句话

senses.en: stadium; a large outdoor sports ground with stands (an indoor arena is 体育馆)

measure.note: 一座体育场 'a stadium' (个 also works)

examples.zh: 体育场离这儿远吗？
examples.en: Is the stadium far from here?
examples.analysis: A 离 B 远 is 'A is far from B': 体育场离这儿远 'the stadium is far from here'. The adjective 远 is the predicate, with no 是, and 吗 makes it a yes/no question.

examples.zh: 周末体育场有活动，人特别多。
examples.en: There's an event at the stadium this weekend, so it'll be really crowded.
examples.analysis: Time, then place, then 有 + event: 周末体育场有活动 'there's an event at the stadium this weekend'. 人特别多 'there are a lot of people' is how Chinese says 'it's crowded'.

examples.zh: 我们在体育场门口见吧。
examples.en: Let's meet at the stadium entrance.
examples.analysis: 在 + place comes before the verb: 在体育场门口见 'meet at the stadium entrance'. 体育场门口 is noun + noun with no 的 needed. 吧 makes the plan a suggestion.

meaning: class monitor; (at work) team or shift leader

senses.en: class monitor: the student who leads a school class
team or shift leader (in a factory or workplace); squad leader (army)

measure.note: 一个班长 (more often 我们班的班长 'our class monitor')

examples.zh: 谁是你们班的班长？
examples.en: Who's the class monitor in your class?
examples.analysis: In a Chinese school class, 班长 is the student chosen to lead the class. 你们班的班长 'your class's monitor': 班 'class' + 的 + 班长. 谁 sits where the answer would go: 小王是班长.

examples.zh: 我上学的时候当过班长。
examples.en: I was class monitor when I was at school.
examples.analysis: 当 (dāng) 'to serve as' + a role: 当班长 'be class monitor'. 过 marks past experience, 'have done (at some point)'. 上学的时候 'back when I was at school' sets the time before the verb.

examples.zh: 这件事你问班长吧，他知道。
examples.en: Ask the class monitor about this. He knows.
examples.analysis: 问 + person is 'ask someone': 问班长 'ask the class monitor'. 这件事 'this matter' comes first as the topic. 吧 softens the instruction into advice, and 他知道 gives the reason.

hook: 班 'class' + 长 (zhǎng) 'head', as in 校长 'principal'.

senses.en: pleasantly cool, a nice feeling (of weather, a place, a breeze), unlike 冷 'cold'

examples.zh: 今天真凉快！
examples.en: It's lovely and cool today!
examples.analysis: 凉快 is a pleasant coolness, unlike 冷 'cold'. As an adjective it follows the subject directly with no 是: 今天 + 真 + 凉快. 真 'really' makes it an exclamation.

examples.zh: 树下凉快，我们去那儿坐一会儿吧。
examples.en: It's cooler under the tree. Let's go and sit there for a while.
examples.analysis: 树下 'under the tree' is the place and 凉快 describes it. Without 很, the bare adjective hints at a contrast: cooler there than here. 坐一会儿 'sit for a while', and 吧 makes it a suggestion.

examples.zh: 下了雨还是不凉快。
examples.en: It rained, but it's still not cool.
examples.analysis: 不凉快 'not cool': 不 negates an adjective directly. 还是 here means 'still', so after 下了雨 'it rained' the sentence says the rain didn't help. In 下了雨, 了 sits between the verb 下 and the object 雨.

collocations.en: to cool off a bit (doubled, used as a verb)

related.en: cool or cold, especially to the touch

senses.en: subway station; metro station

examples.zh: 请问，地铁站怎么走？
examples.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the subway station?
examples.analysis: Place + 怎么走 'how do (I) walk/go' is the usual way to ask for directions: 地铁站怎么走 'how do I get to the subway station?'. 请问 'may I ask' makes it polite.

examples.zh: 我家离地铁站很近，走路五分钟就到。
examples.en: I live close to the subway station. It's just a five-minute walk.
examples.analysis: A 离 B 近 'A is close to B': 我家离地铁站很近. In a plain statement like this, 很 is weaker than English 'very'. 走路五分钟就到 'five minutes on foot and you're there': 就 stresses that's all it takes.

examples.zh: 这儿没有地铁站，得打车。
examples.en: There's no subway station here. We'll have to take a taxi.
examples.analysis: Place + 没有 + thing says something isn't there: 这儿没有地铁站 'there's no subway station here'. 得 (děi) 'have to' + 打车 'take a taxi' gives the result; the subject 'we' is understood.

collocations.en: to go to the subway station

senses.en: air temperature, as in weather reports and talk about the weather

examples.zh: 明天气温多少度？
examples.en: What's the temperature going to be tomorrow?
examples.analysis: 气温 'the temperature' is the topic after 明天 'tomorrow'. 多少度 'how many degrees' is the question, and no verb is needed. An answer would be like 二十度 '20 degrees'.

examples.zh: 最近气温很低，多穿一点儿。
examples.en: Temperatures have been low lately, so put on more layers.
examples.analysis: 气温 takes 低 'low' and 高 'high', as temperatures do in English. 最近 'lately' sets the time. 多穿一点儿 'wear a bit more': 多 before the verb means 'more', and the whole half is friendly advice.

examples.zh: 今天气温不高，挺凉快的。
examples.en: The temperature isn't high today. It's quite nice and cool.
examples.analysis: 气温不高 'the temperature isn't high': 不 + adjective. The second half says how it feels: 挺…的 'quite', so 挺凉快的 is 'quite pleasantly cool'. 气温 is the measured reading; 凉快 is the feeling.

related.en: temperature (of anything: air, water, a room)

senses.en: sneakers; athletic shoes (first for ball games, now any casual sports shoe)

measure.note: 一双球鞋 'a pair of sneakers'

examples.zh: 这些球鞋真好看，在哪儿买的？
examples.en: These sneakers look great. Where did you get them?
examples.analysis: 这些球鞋 'these sneakers': 这些 means 'these' and goes straight before the noun, with no measure word. 在哪儿买的 'where did you buy them?' is 是…的 with 是 dropped, used to ask about a past purchase.

examples.zh: 明天爬山，记得穿球鞋。
examples.en: We're hiking tomorrow, so remember to wear sneakers.
examples.analysis: 穿 is the verb for wearing clothes, shoes and socks: 穿球鞋 'wear sneakers' (hats, glasses and watches take 戴 instead). 记得 + verb 'remember to' makes a friendly reminder. 明天爬山 'tomorrow we hike' gives the reason.

examples.zh: 我的球鞋太脏了，该洗了。
examples.en: My sneakers are really dirty. They need a wash.
examples.analysis: 太脏了 'too dirty': 太 + adjective + 了. 该 + verb + 了 'it's time to…': 该洗了 'they need washing'. The subject 我的球鞋 carries over to the second half without being repeated.

meaning: old age; (before a noun) for older people

senses.en: old age, as a stage of life: 到了老年 'in old age'
(before another noun) of or for older people: 老年人 'seniors', 老年大学

examples.zh: 我奶奶在老年大学学唱歌。
examples.en: My grandma is learning to sing at a university for seniors.
examples.analysis: 老年 describes the noun after it: 老年大学 'a university for older people', common in China, with classes for retired people. 在 + place + verb: 在老年大学学唱歌 'learn singing at…'.

examples.zh: 在这儿，老年人坐公交车不要钱。
examples.en: Here, seniors ride the bus for free.
examples.analysis: 老年 + 人 = 老年人 'older people, seniors', the most common use of 老年. 坐公交车 'ride the bus'. 不要钱 'doesn't cost money' is an everyday way to say 'it's free'. 在这儿 limits the claim to this place.

examples.zh: 人到老年，健康最重要。
examples.en: In old age, health matters most.
examples.analysis: 老年 here is the stage of life, 'old age'. 人到老年 'when people reach old age' is a time clause without a word for 'when'. 最 + adjective is 'most…': 最重要 'most important'.

related.en: old person; close to 老年人

meaning: (of a school or term) to start; start of term

senses.en: (of a school or term) to start: 九月开学 'term starts in September'
(of a student) to start school; go back for a new term
the start of a term (before a noun): 开学第一天 'the first day of term'

examples.zh: 你们学校几号开学？
examples.en: What date does your school start?
examples.analysis: 开学 'school starts' is said of the school or the term, and here it ends the sentence with no object. 几号 'which date' comes before it as the time, and 你们学校 'your school' is the subject.

examples.zh: 下周就开学了，作业还没写完！
examples.en: School starts next week, and I still haven't finished my homework!
examples.analysis: 就…了 says something is coming soon: 下周就开学了 'school starts as soon as next week'. 还没写完 'still haven't finished': verb 写 + 完 'finished', negated with 没.

examples.zh: 开学以后我就没时间了。
examples.en: Once term starts, I won't have any time.
examples.analysis: 开学以后 'after term starts' sets the time; 开学 is the verb 'start' inside a time clause. 就 links the result to it, and 了 at the end marks a change: 没时间了 'won't have time any more'.

collocations.en: opening ceremony of the school year

related.en: to go on holiday; break up for the holidays
to go to school; attend school

senses.en: ugly; unpleasant to look at (clothes, colors, handwriting, a design)

examples.zh: 这件衣服太难看了，别买了。
examples.en: This top is really ugly. Don't buy it.
examples.analysis: 难看 'ugly' is the predicate inside 太…了 'too, really'. 别…了 'don't…' drops a plan already under way: 别买了 'don't buy it after all'. 难看 is blunt, which is fine between friends out shopping.

examples.zh: 我的字太难看了，你来写吧。
examples.en: My handwriting is awful. You write it.
examples.analysis: 字 here is 'handwriting', so 我的字太难看了 is 'my handwriting is awful'. In 你来写吧, 来 before the verb marks taking on a task (as in 我来 'let me do it'), so it means 'you do the writing'; 吧 makes it a request.

examples.zh: 你觉得这个颜色难看？我觉得挺好看的。
examples.en: You think this color is ugly? I think it looks quite nice.
examples.analysis: 难看 and 好看 are opposites. 觉得 + sentence means 'think that…', so 你觉得这个颜色难看 repeats the other person's view as a question, and 我觉得挺好看的 'I think it's quite nice' disagrees gently.

hook: 难 'hard, unpleasant' + 看 'look'; the same pattern gives 难听 'unpleasant to hear'.

meaning: Chinese food; (on schedules and menus) lunch

senses.en: Chinese food; a Chinese meal (the counterpart of 西餐 'Western food')
(on schedules and menus) lunch, in the series 早餐, 中餐, 晚餐; in speech 午饭 is more common

measure.note: 吃一顿中餐 'have a Chinese meal' (顿 counts meals)

examples.zh: 你喜欢吃中餐还是西餐？
examples.en: Do you prefer Chinese food or Western food?
examples.analysis: 中餐 'Chinese food' pairs with 西餐 'Western food', and 还是 offers the choice between them. 喜欢吃 'like eating' is the usual way to say you like a food.

examples.zh: 国外的中餐和中国的不太一样。
examples.en: Chinese food abroad isn't quite the same as in China.
examples.analysis: A 和 B 不太一样 'A and B aren't quite the same'. In 中国的 'the one in China', 中餐 is left out after 的 because it is clear. 不太 'not very' softens the difference.

examples.zh: 在美国住了一年，我特别想吃中餐。
examples.en: After a year living in the US, I really crave Chinese food.
examples.analysis: 想吃中餐 'want to eat Chinese food', here closer to 'crave' or 'miss'. 特别 'really' strengthens it. 住了一年 'lived for a year': the length of time goes after verb + 了.

hook: 中 'China' or 'middle' + 餐 'meal': 'Chinese meal' next to 西餐, 'midday meal' next to 早餐 and 晚餐.
